title: Advanced Senses Arcade
intro: Six rounds on cameras, LiDAR, sound and light. Get them right first try to earn ⭐⭐⭐!

rounds.prompt: What does a single camera pixel report?
options: Three numbers — how much red, green and blue light hit it
A description of the object in view
Only whether it's light or dark, like an IR sensor
rounds.explain: RGB — three separate light measurements per pixel — is the raw data a camera actually captures.

rounds.prompt: What does LiDAR share with an ultrasonic sensor at its core?
options: Both compute distance from the round-trip time of a pulse — light instead of sound
Both need physical contact with the object
rounds.explain: Same time-of-flight idea, different medium — that's the whole relationship between the two.

rounds.prompt: Why can a glass door confuse LiDAR but not necessarily an ultrasonic sensor?
options: Light passes through glass instead of reflecting, so LiDAR can misread it as open space
rounds.explain: Transparency to light is LiDAR's specific blind spot — a real, physical limitation worth knowing.

rounds.prompt: Match each pair — one senses, one does the reverse.
rounds.explain: Four sensors, in two reversed pairs — the same grid or signal idea, running in opposite directions.

rounds.prompt: What does a signal's frequency become once a speaker turns it into sound?
rounds.explain: How fast a wave repeats per second is exactly what your ear hears as a high or low pitch.

rounds.prompt: What's actually inside one RGB LED?
options: Three separate tiny LEDs — red, green, blue — under one lens
A single LED that physically changes colour
rounds.explain: Colour mixing works because three independently controllable LEDs blend in your eye — the same idea a full display scales up.
